doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Booker and Cobb on Washington dance halls and early gigs
summary: Booker adds Mr. Murray's Dance Casino, where Cobb jammed. Cobb jokes about being owed $85 and says he learned playing with older men while pros were in the Army.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: And you had exciting people to stir it to life for you.
Oh, I could see almost anybody I wanted to you know, because they came right to my town.

Well you know I really can’t add very much except I was into listening to a lot of bass players, even though I wanted to play other instruments before I started playing the bass. I can’t add very much to it because I’m just a little bit behind him in years, and we were from Washington. So I was exposed to the same thing almost at the same time, you know? Except there was Mr. Murray’s Dance Casino, which was down the street from where he’s talking about, also added to that. I think I remember him telling me he used to go there and Mr. Murray would let him go there and jam. Is that right? You used to go there?
Yeah. We used to play, but I think I can remember working some place, working for $5 a night and the guy owed me $85 after a while.
That’s a few gigs. About 17 gigs.

But you know I was having fun so and I was learning. That was at a time where the real professional musicians had gone to the Army, you know? So it was like right in that space where I had a chance to play that everybody was left, I had a chance to play with. I mean I’m a young guy playing with older guys, so I got that kind of experience from them.
